newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity falls in tandem with natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity falls in tandem with natgas.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) fell Thursday in tandem with a decline in natural gas market, brokers and traders said.
"They dropped about a buck on a prescheduled basis," said one Houston trader.

The natural gas market was buoyant earlier this week on production shut-in tied to Tropical Storm Josephine and bullish demand outlook for winter storage injection. A considerable amount of Texas' power generation derives from natgas.
But the higher-than-expected data from the American Gas Association's (AGA) latest storage report triggered a sell-off in both the cash and futures natgas markets today.

Late Wednesday, AGA said underground gas inventory in the U.S. rose 94 billion cubic feet last week to 80 percent of capacity. In addition to lower fuel costs, spot ERCOT prices were also pressured by more ERCOT generation returning to service Wednesday.
Lower Colorado River Authority's (LCRA) 430 megawatt (MW) Ferguson gas plant in Marble Falls, Tx., returned to service Wednesday as expected following repairs to a superheater tube.
LCRA's 400 MW Fayette Power Project unit 3 resumed full output after brief cutback due to repairs to a condenser pump.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Friday was quoted at $20.00-$22.00 a megawatt (MWh), down from Wednesday's $22.50-$23.75 range for Thursday delivery.
Off-peak, firm ERCOT power for Friday was again discussed at $12.00.
ERCOT electricity for delivery in 16-hour blocks over the five-business days next week was assessed at $20.00-$21.50.
November ERCOT electricity was still pegged at $20.25, and December ERCOT power was valued at $21.50-$21.75, lower than Wednesday's quote of $22.00.
